_note: Planetocentric latitude, east longitude (0-360 or signed), degrees, LOLA ME frame. 'verify': true means the coordinate comes from memory of the cited source or was approximated and must be checked against the original before being presented as authoritative. 'snapRadiusM': analysis point moved to the highest DEM cell within this radius of the cited coordinate (rim/summit sites only); both are reported.

sites.name: Shackleton–de Gerlache connecting ridge
sites.mission: Artemis III candidate region ("Connecting Ridge")
sites.description: Raised ridge between Shackleton and de Gerlache craters; one of the best-lit spots near the pole.
sites.source: Gläser et al. 2014, Icarus 243, 'Illumination conditions at the lunar south pole using high resolution DTMs from LOLA' (Site 1); NASA Artemis III candidate regions (2022)

sites.name: Shackleton crater rim
sites.mission: Long-studied rim point; Artemis region 'Peak near Shackleton'
sites.description: Rim of the 21 km crater at the pole. High sun incidence, but the crater's own walls shape the horizon.
sites.source: Bussey et al. 2010, Icarus 208 (Point A, 89.68°S 166.0°W)

sites.name: Shackleton crater floor (PSR)
sites.mission: Permanently shadowed region (PSR): cold trap for volatiles
sites.description: Crater floor ~4 km below the rim. The Sun never clears the walls, a control case for 'permanent shadow'.
sites.source: IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature: Shackleton crater centre 89.67°S 129.78°E

sites.name: de Gerlache crater rim
sites.mission: Artemis III candidate region ('de Gerlache Rim')
sites.description: Rim of the 32 km de Gerlache crater, about 50 km from Shackleton.
sites.source: Approximated from IAU Gazetteer crater centre (88.5°S, 87.1°W) and NASA Artemis III region map; not a published point

sites.name: Malapert massif
sites.mission: Artemis III candidate region ('Malapert Massif')
sites.description: A 5 km high mountain on the Earth-facing side; it trades some sunlight for an excellent view of Earth.
sites.source: Sharpton 2014 / NASA Artemis III candidate regions; summit approx. 86.0°S, 2.9°E

sites.name: Mons Mouton (IM-2 Athena)
sites.mission: Intuitive Machines IM-2 'Athena' landing area, March 2025
sites.description: Flat-topped plateau ~160 km from the pole. Athena landed nearby and ended early after tipping over.
sites.source: Intuitive Machines / NASA IM-2 mission reports (landing ≈84.8°S, 29.2°E)

sites.name: Nobile crater western rim
sites.mission: Former VIPER rover target; Artemis III candidate ('Nobile Rim')
sites.description: Western rim of Nobile crater, chosen for rover traverses between lit ridges and shadowed pockets.
sites.source: NASA VIPER mission site selection (2021), approx. western Nobile rim

sites.name: Haworth crater floor (PSR)
sites.mission: Artemis III candidate region ('Haworth') borders this PSR
sites.description: Large permanently shadowed crater. Its floor is a shadow benchmark, so expect almost no direct sunlight.
sites.source: IAU Gazetteer: Haworth crater centre 87.45°S 4.96°W

sites.name: Faustini crater rim
sites.mission: Artemis III candidate region ('Faustini Rim A')
sites.description: Pole-facing rim of the permanently shadowed Faustini crater.
sites.source: Approximated: IAU Gazetteer Faustini centre (87.18°S, 77.0°E) moved ~20 km poleward to the rim; not a published point

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3 (Vikram / Shiv Shakti point)
sites.mission: ISRO Chandrayaan-3 landing, 23 Aug 2023
sites.description: High southern latitude but not polar: ordinary day/night cycle with a low Sun.
sites.source: ISRO; LROC NAC image release (Aug 2023): 69.373°S 32.319°E

sites.name: Apollo 11 (Tranquility Base)
sites.mission: Apollo 11, July 1969, for contrast
sites.description: Equatorial near side: a 14-day day and 14-day night, with Earth fixed high in the sky.
sites.source: LROC / Davies & Colvin 2000 (0.67408°N, 23.47297°E)

sites.name: Chang'e-4 (Von Kármán crater)
sites.mission: CNSA Chang'e-4, first far-side landing, Jan 2019
sites.description: Far side: Earth never rises. All communications go through a relay satellite (Queqiao).
sites.source: Liu et al. 2019, Nature Communications 10:4229 (45.4446°S 177.5991°E)

sites.name: Apollo 12 (Ocean of Storms)
sites.mission: Apollo 12, November 1969
sites.description: Near-equatorial mare site next to Surveyor 3: a two-week day and a two-week night, with Earth high in the sky.
sites.source: Davies & Colvin 2000, JGR 105(E8):20277 (Apollo landing-site coordinates in the lunar mean-Earth frame): 3.01239°S 23.42157°W

sites.name: Apollo 14 (Fra Mauro)
sites.mission: Apollo 14, February 1971
sites.description: Fra Mauro highlands: ordinary equatorial lighting with Earth high overhead.
sites.source: Davies & Colvin 2000, JGR 105(E8):20277 (Apollo landing-site coordinates in the lunar mean-Earth frame): 3.64530°S 17.47136°W

sites.name: Apollo 15 (Hadley–Apennine)
sites.mission: Apollo 15, July 1971
sites.description: Beside Hadley Rille under the Apennine mountains: local relief rises a few degrees, so sunrise and sunset shift slightly.
sites.source: Davies & Colvin 2000, JGR 105(E8):20277 (Apollo landing-site coordinates in the lunar mean-Earth frame): 26.13222°N 3.63386°E

sites.name: Apollo 16 (Descartes highlands)
sites.mission: Apollo 16, April 1972
sites.description: Central highlands: equatorial lighting with Earth high in the sky.
sites.source: Davies & Colvin 2000, JGR 105(E8):20277 (Apollo landing-site coordinates in the lunar mean-Earth frame): 8.97301°S 15.50019°E

sites.name: Apollo 17 (Taurus–Littrow)
sites.mission: Apollo 17, December 1972
sites.description: A valley between massifs on the edge of Mare Serenitatis: steep surrounding terrain delays sunrise and hastens sunset.
sites.source: Davies & Colvin 2000, JGR 105(E8):20277 (Apollo landing-site coordinates in the lunar mean-Earth frame): 20.19080°N 30.77168°E

sites.name: IM-1 Odysseus (near Malapert A)
sites.mission: Intuitive Machines IM-1, NASA CLPS, February 2024
sites.description: The southernmost landing before IM-2: a low Sun and Earth low over the northern horizon.
sites.source: LROC NAC post-landing image release (Feb 2024): ~80.13°S 1.44°E

sites.name: Blue Ghost Mission 1 (Mons Latreille, Mare Crisium)
sites.mission: Firefly Blue Ghost Mission 1, NASA CLPS, March 2025
sites.description: Near-side mare near the eastern limb: Earth sits low in the western sky.
sites.source: Firefly / LROC release (Mar 2025): ~18.56°N 61.81°E

sites.name: IM-3 target (Reiner Gamma swirl)
sites.mission: Intuitive Machines IM-3, NASA CLPS, planned
sites.description: A lunar swirl with a local magnetic field on the western near side; target area, not a landing point.
sites.source: NASA CLPS task order announcement: Reiner Gamma region (approximate centre)

sites.name: Chang'e-3 (Mare Imbrium)
sites.mission: CNSA Chang'e-3 with the Yutu rover, December 2013
sites.description: Northern mare plain: Earth in the southern sky for the whole lunar day.
sites.source: Published post-landing position (CNSA / LROC): ~44.12°N 19.51°W

sites.name: Chang'e-5 (Mons Rümker area)
sites.mission: CNSA Chang'e-5 sample return, December 2020
sites.description: Young mare basalts in Oceanus Procellarum: the most recent sample-return site before Chang'e-6.
sites.source: Published post-landing position (CNSA / LROC): ~43.06°N 51.92°W

sites.name: Chang'e-6 (Apollo basin, far side)
sites.mission: CNSA Chang'e-6, first far-side sample return, June 2024
sites.description: Far side: Earth never rises, so all communication goes through the Queqiao-2 relay.
sites.source: Published post-landing position (CNSA / LROC): ~41.64°S 153.99°W

sites.name: SLIM (near Shioli crater)
sites.mission: JAXA SLIM precision landing, January 2024
sites.description: Near-side highlands: equatorial lighting; the lander came to rest tilted, so its panels faced west.
sites.source: JAXA post-landing position: ~13.316°S 25.251°E

sites.name: Luna 24 (Mare Crisium)
sites.mission: USSR Luna 24 sample return, August 1976
sites.description: Eastern near-side mare: Earth low in the western sky.
sites.source: LROC identification of the Luna 24 lander: ~12.71°N 62.21°E

sites.name: Luna 25 target (Boguslawsky crater)
sites.mission: Roscosmos Luna 25 planned landing site; the spacecraft crashed in August 2023
sites.description: High southern latitude near Boguslawsky crater: a low Sun and Earth low in the north.
sites.source: Roscosmos / IKI pre-launch landing ellipse centre: ~69.55°S 43.54°E
